record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Suppose f belongs to L^2_a(D) and satisfies a lower growth bound |f(z)| >= epsilon (1 - |z|^2)^N throughout D for some positive constants epsilon and N. Must f be cyclic in L^2_a(D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ that are square-integrable with respect to normalized area measure $dA$ on $\mathbb{D}$, i.e.
$$\|f\|^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty.$$
A function $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called cyclic (for the shift operator $M_z$ of multiplication by $z$) if the closed linear span of $\{z^n f:n=0,1,2,\dots\}$ equals $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.

Suppose $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ satisfies the pointwise lower bound
$$|f(z)|\ge \varepsilon\,(1-|z|^2)^N\qquad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{D},$$
for some constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $N>0$. Must $f$ be cyclic in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (posed by H. S. Shapiro) was settled in the negative. Borichev and Hedenmalm (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 761–796, "Harmonic functions of maximal growth: invertibility and cyclicity in Bergman spaces"), and in subsequent work with Volberg on large Bergman spaces, constructed bounded-below (invertible) functions in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ that fail to be cyclic, showing the lower bound $|f(z)|\ge\varepsilon(1-|z|^2)^N$ does not imply cyclicity.

status_evidence.title: Large Bergman spaces: invertibility, cyclicity, and subspaces of arbitrary index
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of invertible non-cyclic elements in weighted Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded-below functions in Bergman-type spaces need not be cyclic, refuting Shapiro's conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Harmonic functions of maximal growth: invertibility and cyclicity in Bergman spaces (Borichev-Hedenmalm, JAMS 1997)
status_evidence.snippet: Borichev and Hedenmalm constructed invertible non-cyclic functions in the Bergman space.
status_evidence.claim: Shapiro's cyclicity lower-bound problem is settled negatively.
